summary: Dedicated pool throughput collapse during mid-window: background snapshotter IO suppresses heartbeats leading to GPU allocation gap
description:
Issue summary:
During the mid-day window on 2026-03-10 our customer VetaHealth observed a sharp throughput collapse in their dedicated GPU pool. The pool reported available capacity but the autoscaler did not attach additional nodes for ~7 minutes, causing application p99 latencies to exceed SLO and a backlog of queued requests.

Impact:
- VetaHealth reported 30% drop in served tokens and sustained p99 latency > 3s for 7 minutes.
- Affected: customer dedicated pool in us-east-1 serving model gptx-13b-quant.
- Business impact: user-facing timeouts and failed inference requests for paid workloads.

Environment:
- Redwood dedicated cluster: prod-us-east, pool id pool-ded-0032.
- Autoscaler: predictive + reactive autoscale policy, min 4 GPUs, max 32 GPUs.
- Sidecar snapshotter enabled for fast warm starts.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Mid-window burst of small short-lived streams from customer app.
2) Background snapshotter ran concurrent NVMe checkpoint write cycles (scheduled retention task).
3) Node-level IO spikes coincided with sidecar heartbeat suppression events; heartbeats from sidecars delayed 20-40s.
4) Scheduler marked ephemeral slots as unresponsive; autoscaler considered current utilization stable and did not request new attachments.
5) Queue length grew; p99 latencies and 5xx rates increased.

Logs / observations:
- Sidecar logs show repeated "heartbeat delayed due to IO wait" entries around 13:02-13:09 UTC.
- Node metrics: write_iops spike to 90% of baseline; disk latency elevated.
- Autoscaler telemetry: no scale-up command issued between 13:01 and 13:08 despite queue crossing scale threshold at 13:02.
- Serving runtime: no kernel errors; models remained pinned.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Disabled snapshotter retention job for pool-ded-0032 (immediate reduction in IO pressure).
- Forced a one-time attach of 4 GPUs to the pool to drain backlog.

Requested next steps:
- Root-cause investigation of interaction between sidecar snapshot IO and heartbeat mechanism.
- Autoscaler logic review to avoid suppression when heartbeats are delayed by transient IO.
- Customer follow-up and RCA with timeline and mitigations.

2026-03-11 11:30 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Proposed mitigations: (1) move snapshotter IO to lower-priority cgroups to avoid starving heartbeat thread, (2) autoscaler policy change to consider queue growth independent of sidecar heartbeat transient failures, (3) add circuit-breaker to temporarily force attachment if queue growth exceeds X for Y seconds.
2026-03-12 08:45 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer notified of temporary mitigations and timeline for runtime patch. Customer requested postmortem and confirmation of no billed retries due to timeouts.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Snapshotter retention duties create high-priority NVMe write load which blocks sidecar heartbeat thread leading scheduler to temporarily misinterpret node liveness.
Repro in staging: Synthetic snapshot writer + short-stream flood reproduces delayed heartbeat and autoscaler non-action. Verified disk latency as causal factor.

Autoscaler observed queue threshold but deferred scale because sidecar heartbeats delayed caused slot state to be inconsistent; scheduler didn't mark slots as 'available' for new attachments even though GPUs reported idle.
Telemetry gaps: heartbeat latency is currently only tracked as last-seen timestamp; need histogram of heartbeat delays to correlate with IO metrics.
Risk assessment: If snapshotter IO runs align with customer bursts, repeated incidents possible. Medium-high risk for dedicated pools with heavy snapshot retention.

Proposed fix list: 1) Patch sidecar to run heartbeat on isolated thread with IO-resilient settings; 2) Add autoscaler override when queue growth sustained > threshold; 3) Add scheduling rule to deprioritize background snapshotter IO on production pool nodes.
resolution: In progress - temporary mitigations applied (snapshotter retention job disabled and forced attach). Platform engineering opened runtime PR to harden sidecar heartbeat and SRE proposed autoscaler policy changes. Next actions: merge runtime PR, roll out to canary, monitor. Postmortem scheduled after deploy. Customer will receive credit for affected minutes pending postmortem confirmation.
